name: Calangute Beach
description: The largest and most popular beach in North Goa stretching 7 km, lined with beach shacks and water-sports operators offering parasailing, jet-skiing, and banana boat rides.

name: Baga Beach
description: Vibrant North Goa beach known for its lively shack culture, nightlife strip, and water sports. The Baga River mouth creates a calm backwater pool perfect for early morning walks.

name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
description: UNESCO World Heritage baroque church completed in 1605, housing the mortal remains of St. Francis Xavier in an ornate mausoleum of jasper, marble, and gilt-wood carved panels.

name: Se Cathedral
description: Largest church in Asia, built by the Portuguese between 1562 and 1619 in Portuguese-Gothic style, featuring the famous Golden Bell, one of the finest bells in the world.

name: Dudhsagar Waterfalls
description: Majestic four-tiered waterfall on the Goa-Karnataka border plunging 310 m, one of India tallest falls. Best experienced after monsoon when the milky-white cascade is at full flow.

name: Fort Aguada
description: Impressive 17th-century Portuguese sea fort built in 1612, offering panoramic views of the Arabian Sea and Mandovi River estuary from its iconic single-towered lighthouse.

name: Anjuna Flea Market
description: Legendary Wednesday market running since the 1960s hippie era, offering Rajasthani textiles, silver jewellery, Kashmiri shawls, local spices, and hand-crafted Goan souvenirs.

name: Palolem Beach
description: Crescent-shaped South Goa beach lined with colourful huts and palm trees, known for calmer seas, dolphin-watching boat trips, kayaking, and spectacular sunset views.
